title: How long “should” it take to create a project with AI assistance?
author: Codingology
selftext:
I know this is a very subjective question but I’d like to see through the comments the average time span you guys took / are taking to make a game. Obviously it depends by the vastness of the content, but I feel we could find an average.  
It’s been 1 month and half for me since I started using Claude for the coding, however, some 3d models and the UI was ready years ago, so I’m working with things already done. Realistically it would have taken me maybe 2 months and an half / 3 to be in the current state that I am if I had started from 0.  
To finish the game I believe it will take me yet another 2 months. So let’s say that for me it is about 6 months time. What about you?

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
...I think the bones of a good game can probably be set in about a week, ish.  

The benefit is that you can go into a lot of integration right away to see what does and doesn't work in terms of the audio/visual experience. Prior to AI, you couldn't really do that; everything had to be just placeholder art and sound, and you had to just hope the final product would look good. 

The pitfall is that having a good set of bones and integrations can make it tempting to not finish cooking the game. 'Oh, \[X\] Steam even is happening. Well, fck it, may as well push the crap out since it technically is playable right now.' 

  
After you've got the bones made, it will take months of design work, reworks, testing and content creation to actually build out a good game.

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body: Your estimate sounds honest, and the part people usually leave out is what you mention: assets you already had. AI speeds up the code a lot, but the last stretch (balancing, bugs only real players find, store page, trailer) runs at about the same speed as it always did. A useful way to plan is to set a date for the first time a stranger plays it, not for "done", and plan the rest from what that playtest shows.
